strengths: Novel application: First to use primitives as fundamental units for large-scale 3D urban scene generation, opening a new research direction distinct from voxel-based approaches

Well-motivated technical contributions: Cholesky-based parameterization elegantly solves orientation sign ambiguity with clear mathematical justification; disentangled latent structure enables ground-conditioned generation without fine-tuning
Practical benefits clearly demonstrated: 3× memory reduction (2.52 vs 8.00 MB), resolution-independent representation, intuitive instance-level editing operations (translation, rotation, scaling)
Comprehensive experimental framework: Rigorous train-test split with 5m overlap prevention, 61,913 training poses, multiple evaluation metrics, ablation studies on key design choices
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Well-structured paper with informative visualizations, 26 pages of supplementary material with detailed implementation specifics, enabling reproducibility
Versatile downstream applications: Inpainting, outpainting, and photo-realistic synthesis work without fine-tuning by leveraging latent manipulation
Quantitative improvements: Significant gains in FID (156.24→51.30), generation precision/recall, and qualitative advantages over baseline visualizations are compelling
weaknesses: Critical evaluation limitation: Only SemCity baseline compared; no comparisons with other semantic scene generation methods (CC3D, Layout2Scene, SLEDGE, Urban Architect, etc.) cited but not evaluated, undermining claims of superiority

Single-dataset evaluation severely limits generalizability: Authors explicitly acknowledge evaluation restricted to KITTI-360 due to data scarcity; raises questions about robustness to different urban layouts, environments, or annotation styles

Generation metrics reliability concerns: Paper acknowledges precision/recall highly sensitive to batch size, sample diversity, and neighborhood size k; Fig. 9 shows precision ranging 0.0-0.75 depending on configuration—metric instability undermines confidence in generation quality claims

Reconstruction comparison is convoluted and misleading: SemCity with 1M query points achieves mIoU=93.81 (superior to PrITTI's 70.27), yet framing emphasizes the incomplete 400K baseline; voxelization of primitives introduces approximation error not present in voxel baseline

Limited practical scope: Static scenes only (no dynamics); coarse primitive geometry acknowledged to limit fine detail capture; unclear scalability beyond 64m×64m FOV; cannot model real-world dynamics essential for autonomous driving applications

Insufficient failure analysis: Figure 10 shows floating objects and disconnected outpainting, but failures under-analyzed; no quantitative failure rate, systematic study of failure conditions, or guidance on when method is applicable

Incomplete ablation studies: Cholesky vs. Quaternion tested on synthetic single-object data (generalization unclear); no ablation on fixed object counts, padding strategy, latent dimensions, or architectural choices; loss weight scheme (Table 3) appears ad-hoc without justification

Missing critical experiments: No perceptual/human evaluation validating visual quality claims; no comparison with indoor scene generation methods or alternative primitive encodings; FID computed on 256² 2D semantic maps is indirect proxy for 3D quality

strengths: Novel application of primitives to large-scale 3D semantic scene generation with clear motivation (memory efficiency, editability, compositionality)
Mathematically sound Cholesky-based parameterization that elegantly resolves quaternion sign ambiguity
Comprehensive technical execution including disentangled latent design enabling multiple downstream applications without fine-tuning
Demonstrates 3× memory reduction compared to baseline while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality
Well-written paper with detailed supplementary material and thorough implementation specifications
weaknesses: CRITICAL: Evaluated on single dataset (KITTI-360) only; paper itself acknowledges this is the only dataset with dense primitive annotations, severely limiting generalization claims and CVPR suitability

Baseline comparison concerns: SemCity reached only epoch 18 vs. PrITTI's 300 epochs on same hardware; SemCity at full resolution (1M queries) achieves 93.81 mIoU vs. claimed gains; missing comparisons with hierarchical voxel methods and SLEDGE

Inherent representation limitations: primitives are coarse, fail on fine-grained details (lamps on poles, fences); ground surfaces rasterized then extruded lose polygon detail; geometric fidelity unresolved for precision-critical applications

Evaluation methodology fragility: precision/recall metrics (Fig. 9) vary dramatically with sampling strategy and neighborhood size k, undermining robustness claims; voxelization introduces approximation error; no direct primitive-space metrics
Static scenes only—no dynamics, severely limiting autonomous driving applicability mentioned as key use case
Cholesky parameterization ablation uses synthetic data only; no full KITTI-360 ablation validating actual generation impact; quaternion baseline may not be properly optimized
Limited scope: only 11 object categories, category-specific loss weights indicate heavy dataset tuning, no analysis of unseen categories or cross-dataset transfer
Downstream applications (inpainting/outpainting) demonstrated qualitatively only; no metrics for consistency; failures show 'weakly connected or semantically inconsistent' completions

Missing sensitivity analysis: multiple hyperparameters and design choices (patch sizes, loss weights, latent dimensions) but no systematic ablation; scatter-mean operation lossy but alternatives unexplored
No code/model release mentioned; reproducibility requires custom KITTI-360-specific preprocessing; depends on external pre-trained ControlNet for photo-realistic synthesis

strengths: Novel primitive-based formulation: First to leverage 3D primitives (cuboids, ellipsoids) as fundamental units for large-scale semantic scene generation, addressing real limitations of voxel grids (memory, fixed resolution, editability).

Strong technical contributions: Cholesky-based parameterization elegantly resolves quaternion sign ambiguity with rigorous mathematical justification; disentangled latent structure (zG, zO) enables flexible manipulation without additional supervision.

Comprehensive evaluation: Multiple complementary metrics (IoU, AP3D, FID, IS, Precision, Recall); thorough ablations with synthetic data; fair baseline comparison with SemCity at multiple resolutions; detailed sensitivity analysis.

Practical demonstrations: Scene inpainting/outpainting without fine-tuning, intuitive object-level editing (rotation, scaling, translation), controllable generation, ground-conditioned synthesis, and photo-realistic street-view integration showcase real utility.
Significant efficiency gains: 3× memory reduction (2.52 MB vs. 8.0 MB) with comparable or superior generation quality; resolution-independent representation.

Transparency and reproducibility: Extensive supplementary material with architectural details, training procedures, loss specifications, dataset construction; honest discussion of limitations with failure case analysis.
weaknesses: Single-dataset evaluation: Restricted to KITTI-360, the only dataset with dense primitive annotations for large outdoor scenes, limiting generalization claims and raising questions about domain transfer.

Reconstruction quality comparable, not superior: AP3D=62.12 is comparable to voxel baseline; generation metrics show clear improvement, but reconstruction advantage is overstated—claim of 'superior reconstruction performance' should be nuanced.

Geometric fidelity limitations: Coarse primitives inherently limit detail; fine-grained structures (lamps on poles, fences) problematic; rasterized ground representation constrained by resolution, reducing applicability for precision-demanding tasks.
Static scene limitation: Cannot model temporal dynamics, significantly restricting applicability in autonomous driving simulations and scenarios requiring scene evolution.

Limited baseline comparison: Only compared against SemCity (voxel-based); while understandable given this is the first primitive-based method, comparison with at least one additional outdoor generation approach would strengthen claims.
Outpainting failure modes: Explicit failure when conditioning blocks contain large empty regions, limiting practical applicability for extending sparse scenes.

Evaluation metric sensitivity: Precision/recall metrics highly sensitive to distance thresholds, sample counts, and neighborhood sizes (acknowledged in Fig. 9), raising concerns about robustness of reported generative performance.

strengths: Novel primitive-based representation using Cholesky parameterization is elegant, memory-efficient, and semantically meaningful compared to voxel grids
Strong experimental validation with consistent improvements over recent baselines (SemCity, PDD, XCube) across multiple metrics (IoU, Precision, Recall, FID)
Comprehensive framework supporting diverse downstream applications (scene editing, inpainting, outpainting, photo-realistic synthesis) with well-designed manipulation strategies
Well-engineered technical approach with separate ground/object VAE architecture and thoughtfully designed loss formulations combining raster and vector losses
Grounded in real-world data (KITTI-360) with implementation details, code release promise, and extensive supplementary material supporting reproducibility
Thorough ablation studies examining Cholesky vs. quaternion encodings, joint vs. separate training, and detailed precision/recall evaluation across neighborhoods
weaknesses: Limited novelty in diffusion architecture - relies on standard DiT [68] with main contribution being representation and application rather than architectural innovation
Evaluation limited to single dataset (KITTI-360 outdoor urban scenes) with no validation on other urban datasets (ScanNet, Structured3D) or indoor environments, limiting generalizability claims
Unfair baseline comparison: PrITTI trained on real KITTI-360 while baselines trained on synthetic CarlaASC dataset; no ablation of baselines on KITTI-360 for fair architectural comparison
High sensitivity to evaluation protocol (Fig. 10) with substantially different precision/recall results between distance-threshold and farthest-pose sampling, raising robustness concerns

Primitive representation inherently constrains geometric fidelity (acknowledged limitation); failure cases with floating/disconnected objects (Fig. 11) and ground rasters losing fine structural details are not thoroughly analyzed
Semantic consistency issues evident in generated scenes (Figs. 9, 15) with misplaced objects and limited soft constraints on spatial plausibility; no explicit physics or co-occurrence modeling
Missing comparisons to recent mesh-based, point-cloud generation methods and hierarchical VAE approaches; unfair to compare against methods with different training data
No quantitative user studies validating perceived realism or editability; loss weight design choices and latent dimension selection lack justification or ablation
Incomplete analysis of memory savings vs. voxel methods (claimed but not quantified); scalability to large scenes (256m × 256m) shows degraded quality with no systematic analysis

strengths: Novel Cholesky-based parameterization for compact 3D primitive encoding is mathematically well-motivated and enables intuitive instance-level editing operations
Two-stage architecture (Layout VAE + LDM) is technically sound with clear separation of spatial layout learning and generative modeling
Demonstrated practical advantages in memory efficiency (2.52 MB vs. 8.00 MB for SemCity) while maintaining comparable reconstruction quality
Primitive-based representation naturally supports controllable scene editing with operations like object rotation, scaling, and translation that voxel methods lack
Comprehensive technical documentation with extensive supplementary results and multiple downstream applications demonstrated
weaknesses: Fundamental geometric fidelity limitation to simple cuboids and ellipsoids cannot represent complex real-world object shapes (diverse vehicles, irregular buildings, intricate vegetation); Figure 11(a) shows failure cases with floating/disconnected objects

Quantitative generation results (Table 3: Precision=0.807, Recall=0.545) fail to convincingly demonstrate superiority over baselines; claims of 'state-of-the-art quality' unsupported by metrics showing competitive but not superior performance

Unfair baseline comparisons using fundamentally different representations (primitives vs. voxels) without normalizing for architectural differences; unclear whether improvements stem from representation choice or other factors

Severely limited evaluation scope restricted to single dataset (KITTI-360 urban driving); no generalization demonstrated on other 3D scene datasets or domains, leaving extensibility to other environments completely unvalidated

Evaluation methodology highly sensitive to hyperparameters (distance threshold τ, neighborhood size k); Figure 10 shows metric variation across methods depending on protocol with no principled justification for chosen parameters
Fixed semantic categories from KITTI-360 limit flexibility; Section G acknowledges inability to support open-vocabulary generation or extension to new semantic structures without complete retraining
Missing systematic failure analysis and quantitative failure rate despite documented failure modes; no discussion of percentage of generated scenes requiring post-processing or manual fixing
Photo-realistic street-view synthesis claims (Figure 27) not convincingly demonstrated with visible artifacts and unrealistic object appearances; this downstream application appears preliminary

Missing ablations on key design choices (Cholesky vs. quaternions relegated to supplementary material) and VAE+LDM architecture alternatives; limited engagement with concurrent primitive-based and scene generation work
Reproducibility concerns including promised-but-unavailable code, complex dataset preprocessing, and unjustified hyperparameter choices (loss weights); no timing benchmarks despite efficiency claims

strengths: Novel primitive-based representation effectively addressing memory efficiency (2.5MB vs 8MB) and compositionality limitations of voxel methods
Comprehensive two-stage pipeline with well-designed LVAE and diffusion architecture, including clever Choleskey parameterization for orientation handling
Strong Stage 1 reconstruction results demonstrating superior quality compared to voxel baselines (SemCity, PDD, XCube)
Versatile downstream applications (editing, inpainting, outpainting, rendering) enabled by the representation, with clear qualitative advantages in object-level manipulations
Thorough experimental validation with multiple baselines, ablation studies on key design choices (Choleskey vs quaternion, joint vs separate training)
Significantly faster generation and reduced memory footprint enabling practical deployment
Clear presentation with comprehensive supplementary material and promise of code release for reproducibility
weaknesses: Evaluation limited to single dataset (KITTI-360, urban driving scenario); no validation on other environments or geographic regions restricts generalizability claims
Marginal quantitative improvements in precision/recall metrics (Table 3) with acknowledged high sensitivity to implementation details, implementation parameters, and neighborhood size
Geometric fidelity limitations remain unresolved: primitives struggle with fine details (poles, fences), and paper lacks systematic failure mode analysis by category
Evaluation methodology concerns: precision/recall metrics acknowledged as brittle, IoU-based metrics potentially biased toward voxel methods, no perceptual metrics or user studies
Inconsistent scene quality in outpainting with visible seams at block transitions and disconnected/floating objects; no explicit geometric consistency constraints during generation
Limited technical justification for design choices: why cuboids+ellipsoids specifically (no ablation), ad-hoc category-specific loss weights (Table 5), unclear joint latent concatenation implications
Scene consistency issues including ground surface discontinuities across boundaries and occasional semantic inconsistencies between ground and object placements
Incomplete baseline comparisons: only voxel methods compared; missing comparisons with recent primitive-based or diffusion-based scene generation approaches
Fixed semantic vocabulary from KITTI-360 and fixed ~64m×64m scene sizes limit scalability; unclear generalization to novel geographic regions or semantic compositions
Limited pipeline novelty: LVAE+diffusion framework is standard; primary contribution is representation rather than generation mechanism
